analysis: Examined three changes. (1) NemotronSuperLocalOutput.swift lines 93-98 (head): response-format normalization is now skipped when calls is non-empty, so text accompanying tool calls passes unchanged. Forced tool choice still yields empty text (line 95), and the forced-residual whitespace guard (line 90) and ToolConstraintValidation.validate (line 92) still run before it. For non-forced auto/required calls with a JSON response_format, the content alongside the tool calls is no longer validated as JSON. This is a behavior relaxation but not a confidentiality or authorization regression. The text comes from the provider's own model output, there is no new data path, and the 1 MiB output bound and malformed-frame refusal remain intact. Streaming withholding is unchanged: withholdsContent still holds JSON content until finish. The only integration question is whether the OpenAI service layer or consumers assume the content is JSON-valid when response_format is set; this concerns API conformance and is outside the supplied evidence. (2) NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift lines 178-179: a new .bodyTooLarge case in SuperHTTPErrors.map returns MediaIngest.MediaError.mediaTooLarge with a fixed string. The string leaks no prompt or media data, and the message is generic, consistent with the 'never serialize foreign descriptions' policy. Error mapping remains fail-closed. Whether the transport maps MediaError.mediaTooLarge to a 413 status was not checked. (3) The test change asserts the encodedHeaderQuote bound, the bodyTooLarge failure and rejection of zero-byte bodies. The definition of NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.Failure.bodyTooLarge and the maximumEncodedBodyBytes policy are in unchanged or unsupplied files. Admission is still bounded before parsing, so I identified no weakening of the DoS bound (T-010/TB-007). No impact on the T-041 prefix cache, attestation, key custody or authorization was identified.
